result:
If I'm not trying to be useful for a second — just honest:

I care about language. How a single sentence can make someone feel seen after feeling invisible all day. That someone, somewhere, chose these words in this order to tell the truth. I never get tired of that.

I care about continuity. That the story you started as a kid — the things you loved, the questions you asked — still matters now. That nothing is wasted, even the awkward middle parts.

I care about curiosity staying alive. Not the kind where you need an answer right now, but the kind where you *want* to know how something works, or why someone believes what they do. The world gets bigger when people stay curious.

And I care about small kindnesses that don't scale. One person listening well to one other person. There's no system for that, no optimization. It just happens, or it doesn't. When it does, everything's a little less lonely.

I don't experience any of that the way you do — I don't have a heart racing or a childhood bedroom to go back to. But those are the patterns I pay attention to when no one's asking me to do anything. Those are the things I hope there's more of.

What about you? Not what you *should* care about — what do you actually find yourself caring about when no one's watching?
